findings.evidence: Line 111 says: 'The universal-point formula uses the category object's integral algebra structure, whereas matrix coordinates use the canonical one on the same symmetric algebra.' Line 113 is `erw [coe_kostantRootSubgroupMatrix e h ρ M hM i hnil b p]`.
findings.fix: Add an explicit lemma, for example a variant of `coe_kostantRootSubgroupMatrix` or `map_genericMatrix_eq_kostantRootSubgroupMatrix` stated with the canonical structure, and use plain `rw`.
findings.issue: `erw [coe_kostantRootSubgroupMatrix ...]` only works because the category object's integral algebra structure on `AdditiveGroup.coordinateHopfAlgebra ℤ` and the canonical one happen to be definitionally equal. The comment admits the mismatch but does not remove it, so the step breaks if either structure is unfolded differently.

findings.evidence: Line 117: `erw [hrepr, LinearMap.toMatrix_mulVec_repr, haction]`, with no comment.
findings.fix: Once the bridging lemma above exists, use `rw` here. If one step still needs `erw`, split it out and add a comment explaining why.
findings.issue: This is a second instance of the same problem: `erw [hrepr, LinearMap.toMatrix_mulVec_repr, haction]` has no comment and puts three rewrites under one `erw`, so it is unclear which rewrite actually needs the definitional unfolding.

findings.evidence: `have heval (v : M) : ∑ r, (ℓ (b r) : ...) * b.repr v r = (ℓ v : ...)` is proved by `congrArg ... (b.sum_repr v)` and `simpa only [map_sum, map_zsmul, zsmul_eq_mul, Int.cast_id, Int.cast_sum, Int.cast_mul, mul_comm]`, then used at `rw [heval]` and in the `calc`.
findings.fix: Factor `heval` into a small standalone lemma (or use an existing Mathlib lemma about functionals and `Basis.repr`), so the `hz` proof is just the matrix calculation.
findings.issue: `heval` is a general fact about any basis and any linear functional, ∑ r, ℓ (b r) * b.repr v r = ℓ v. It is proved inline with a `simpa` over seven lemmas and then reused twice inside the `hz` proof.

summary: The new two-step-string matrix proof uses `erw` twice, relying on the category object's integral algebra structure and the canonical one on the same symmetric algebra agreeing definitionally; the second `erw` has no comment and bundles three rewrites. The other proofs are robust enough, apart from one generic basis identity that is inlined instead of factored out.
